data.narrative:
Vertical Aerospace is a public-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector that has raised $50M to date. The relevant peer universe comprises eight private companies in the same sector, including Joby Aviation, Archer Aviation, Waymo, Wayve, and Zipline. No public comparables exist within the Drones & Autonomous space, limiting traditional public market benchmarking.

The peer-median method was not applicable to this analysis. The sector contains seven same-sector peers overall, but filtering for stage alignment and valuation tier consistency yielded fewer than three datapoints—the minimum threshold for reliable triangulation. Attempting to broaden the filter to all-sector medians would introduce significant distortion given the heterogeneity in business models, technology readiness, and capital intensity across the broader universe.

Given the constraints imposed by peer sparsity and stage mismatch, a rigorous valuation range cannot be established from the data provided. The absence of both public comparables and a sufficiently dense cohort of private peers at comparable stages renders the standard triangulation framework inapplicable here. A defensible valuation would require either (1) expansion into adjacent sectors with comparable capital and timeline profiles, (2) acquisition of additional private transaction data within Drones & Autonomous, or (3) deployment of alternative methods such as DCF or precedent transaction analysis with explicit disclosure of methodological limitations.
